vault._note: Used only when DENISSE_VAULT is unset and settings.vault() finds nothing; home-relative.

context.preamble: Read-only. Facts here outrank your assumptions; anything missing is unknown.
context._parts: In order: read note -> body (drop front matter) -> section -> strip_heading -> known_only (drop areas whose lines carry unknown_marker) -> bullets (keep the last N if last).

digest._note: python -m atrium digest [--since HOURS] [--dry]: what happened on this laptop since the last digest. Sections are written in the order listed and a section with no lines is left out. When no section with counts_as_activity has a line, nothing is written (the state still moves on). log/review are repo-relative; state_file and globs are vault-relative.

sections.title: Orchestra
sections._events: Orchestra's runner.log line format: '<ISO time> <WORD> <task>[:] <rest>'. WORD -> the label it is listed under (in this order), or -> {what <rest> starts with: label} when the outcome is in the rest; other words and outcomes are ignored.
sections.spend: - spend: ${total:.2f} over {runs} run(s) with a known cost

sections.title: Vault
sections._skip_prefixes: Subjects starting with one of these are left out: the digests' own commits, so a digest never reports the last one.

sections.title: Queue
sections.draft: - needs Chuen: approve draft {task} (Queue: draft -> auto)

install_digest._note: atrium/install_digest.py: the hourly Windows scheduled task for the digest. Prints the command; only --register runs it. python and script are repo-relative.

live._note: python -m atrium live: the laptop's own live Atrium page (atrium/live.py, page in atrium/live_page/). Read-only: it serves what atrium/snapshot.py collects and never writes. host must be one of loopback. Work happens only while a browser tab holds the event stream open: every poll_s the watched files are stat'ed and the data rebuilt when one changed (or refresh_s passed, for limits that lift with the clock).
live._watch: review: globs inside .review (a folder counts its entries and their subfolders); vault: vault-relative files.
live.title: Atrium Live
live.subtitle: What's happening in the background
live._agents: One bar and one timeline row each, in this order. lane = the Orchestra lane (snapshot usage rows); colour = the accent used everywhere that agent appears.
live._needs: Overlaps (two agents in one file, from cursors below) come first: they need you before a merge does.
live._cursors: atrium/cursors.py: one pointer per running task, in its agent's colour, on its task row and on the file its worktree touched last; every touched file listed once (shared first, then newest, at most max_files) with who is in it. A file two agents both touch is an overlap: one warning per file, also in Needs you. worktrees = the runner's worktree folder ({repo_parent}, {repo_name} of this checkout; orchestra/runner.py WORKTREES); touched = committed since merge-base with base_ref + uncommitted + untracked, read-only (git_env: no index refresh). Ignored: the runner's own orchestra/config.json <runner_ignore_key> prefixes when use_runner_ignores, plus ignore (globs on the path or the file name). Cached per worktree for refresh_s, so the page's existing loop is the only one. page: the keys sent to app.js (pixel sizes, glide time); the glide is one CSS transition, none under prefers-reduced-motion or when a hidden tab comes back.

timeline._classes: result -> colour class (ok/warn/bad); a run still going is drawn in its agent's colour.

live._study: Week notes written of weeks filed: every week_glob folder under each module in root (vault-relative) is filed; it is written when it holds a note_glob file of at least written_min_chars characters.

install_live._note: atrium/install_live.py: starts the live page hidden at logon and adds shortcuts that open it. schtasks ONLOGON needs admin on this laptop (9 Nov 2026: Access is denied), so it uses the per-user Startup folder. folder = a .NET Environment.SpecialFolder name. Prints the PowerShell only; --register runs it. python and script are repo-relative.
